newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Ex-Bangladesh PM attacks India insurgency pact.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Bangladesh PM attacks India insurgency pact.

text.p: Bangladesh's former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia has attacked a recent agreement between India and Bangladesh to combat insurgencies along their border, local newspapers reported on Monday.
The papers quoted her as accusing New Delhi of planning to use Bangladesh territory to suppress domestic rebellions, something she said Bangladeshi people would never allow.

"India is planning to use Bangladesh as a corridor to suppress rebellion in its various parts. But (we) shall not allow use of Bangladesh for crushing those fighting for independence," the Bhorer Kagoj daily quoted her as saying.

"(Our) people will never allow Bangladesh to be used to suppress the struggle for liberation there," the Daily Star newspaper quoted her as telling a meeting of her opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP).
Bangladesh and India recently agreed to work together to quell insurgency along their borders.
Senior government officials from both sides met in New Delhi last week to work out modalities for a joint fight against insurgency.

A spokesman for Bangladesh's foreign office declined to comment directly on Khaleda's accusation, but said Dhaka had agreed to cooperate with India "in taking proper measures to combat and contain insurgency and terrorism." India has long faced a bloody insurgency in its seven north eastern states bordering Bangladesh, Burma and China.
Tribal rebels in Bangladesh's Chittagong Hill Tracts, bordering India, have been fighting a bush war since 1973 that has claimed more than 8,500 lives.
Khaleda lost to Sheikh Hasina's Awami League in elections last June.
